newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices edge up ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices edge up ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: Danish bond prices edged up on Wednesday, in a market still pondering its direction ahead of the next few days' U.S. data and renewed fears of a Fed rate rise.
"There will be a good deal of attention on the United States in the days up to the FOMC meeting next Tuesday," a dealer said.
At 1215 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.04 basis point from Tuesday's close, at 111.32, yielding 6.28 percent, in turnover of 1.6 billion crowns.
Its June future fell 0.02 point to 111.04, with 101 contracts traded.
The forthcoming benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 was up 0.06 to 103.92, yielding 6.46 percent, in turnover of 0.5 billion crowns.
The gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund stood at 57 basis points and the 2007-bund gap was 75 bp.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.12 point, to 89.75 amid foreign interest in mortage-backed paper for which Wednesday's net foreign buying was around 0.5 billion crowns.
The crown traded at 3.8067 per mark, off its earlier 3.8060 but firming from Tuesday's 3.8075. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
